items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: I thought a while and I made the song out of it. I threw it on the side and never worried about it. Today I realized that that kind of stuff goes.

ctx.x: I knew his brother would sing a lot of Creole songs.

Yeah, well that's what I'm coming to. And he said, I'll have to translate it for you because he said it in Creole. It means, who told you I was going there? I told him nobody said you was going there. I told him in French, nobody was going there. And from that, I just started and started to play with a little tune you know. I'll compose myself. And from that we made a song. You see? And the song goes like this in Creole. It says, who told you I was going there? It speaks as though two people were talking, two…
Yeah, that's right. Some of those things would sell good now. They could make up the stuff.
Some of them had been students of Xavier. I thought I mean Xavier. That was given out to Xavier or Dillard? Xavier. Xavier. Yeah, that's what I meant. That was given out Xavier. That was December 32.

Yeah. And of course, like those fellows would be the... Now as far as jazz is concerned, I used to play a lot of jazz on the piano, you know? Oh yes. But I never did fancy very much of piling up in those... the red light districts. I never said to go around there. I didn't want to worry about that at all. Although, much of my colleagues used to play. Piku and all of them used to play.
Professor Minetta's told us about those. He played at the tuxedo dance hall and some of the houses and all too. Yes. Yes. He's told us all about that. But I used to play for private people.
